Simply, probably, I cannot claim what his thoughts were, but I assume that he joined for the simple reason to protect himself against threats, possible problems that he might have in connection with his family, because he was living in an environment in which 95 per cent of the inhabitants were Muslims and they were all members of the SDA, with the exception of a small number who were members of the civilian forum.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: He was entrusted with organising the SDS plebiscite in Kozarac, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not present, but I heard that that was so, that they organised a plebiscite.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your brother was entrusted with organising that plebiscite -- is that not what you testified to earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably he was given such an assignment. I do not know who gave him this assignment because, as I said, I was not living on the territory of Prijedor and I was not a member of the SDS in Prijedor. I heard that they had organised this plebiscite in the Orthodox church in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you are saying that you did not have personal knowledge of a great deal of what was going on in the opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot know everything. I do not know about this thing. I was not following everything that was happening. I was not a politician or anyone with any kind of a duty to follow developments. I attended -- I went to Kozarac prior to the war for one simple reason, to see my mother, my family, to build these business premises. I wanted to earn a living, to go into business. That is all. Everything that I heard in the process I have told you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In addition to organising this plebiscite, your brother also held a series of political positions in Kozarac, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was Secretary of the local office, the Local Commune.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: He was also President of the party in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not a political function.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: He was also President of the party in Kozarac, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how somebody can be the President of a party when there are not enough inhabitants for membership. At the time in Kozarac there were not so many inhabitants. This is the first time for me to hear that he was President of the party. I know that he was Secretary of the Local Commune, that he worked in the Red Cross, that he was in the Kozarac police when the police station was formed in Kozarac. That is all.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: He was also a representative to the Prijedor Municipal Assembly, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On behalf of the Local Commune, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this may be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the witness is brought in, there is a redaction that is required at 15.40.20 which I believe your Honour already knows about.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, is that the one you gave me?

utterances.speaker: MISS FEATHERSTONE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, that has been signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, while we are waiting, this mountain over which the unfortunate people were taken and then the incident occurred, does that appear on this map that you have given us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I see Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can your Honour see Paljenik? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: It is your pronunciation that misleads me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Paljenik, I am told.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is the very light, the white, area that you see to the -----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: The radio towers?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Exactly. Right there. That is the top of the mountain. Yes, sir. The whole region is known as Vlasic. That is the particular mountain to which it refers

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We agree.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: While you were gone, Mr. Wladimiroff, Mr. Kay was taking us through all of these names here and he was pronouncing them so well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I missed a lot of fun!

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. Miss Hollis, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic, before the break we were discussing the political activities in which your brother Dusko was involved. In fact, your brother Dusko was more involved in the Serb efforts in opstina Prijedor than merely belonging to the SDS, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What efforts?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The Serb efforts to consolidate themselves and to prepare for the actions that were to occur beginning in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did your brother Dusko not discourage other Serbs in the Kozarac area from co-operating with Muslims at sentry points in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What town?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs did not have checkpoints in Kozarac, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did your brother not attempt to discourage Serbs from co-operating with non-Serbs at these sentry points in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother -- Serbs in Kozarac were not minors so that they had to be instructed what to do.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did your brother Dusko not try to organise assignments for the Serbs for when fighting broke out in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What assignments?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Assignments that Serbs would carry out when fighting began in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did your brother Dusko not attempt to acquire weapons for himself and other Serbs in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So if your brother was involved in any of these efforts, you were not aware of them, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not aware of that, but many Serbs in Kozarac were -- had good relations with Muslims in Kozarac. I doubt whether anybody attempted, offered the Serbs in Kozarac, I mean, in the centre of Kozarac to take that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So if your brother were involved in these efforts you did not assist him in any of these efforts, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Though you say you were not aware of these efforts, you were aware, were you not, that your brother fully supported the creation of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a member of SDS, nothing special, like everybody else.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You are aware, are you not, that he fully supported the idea of a Serb state for Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a member of SDS.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is what the SDS wanted, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course it wanted that all Serbs live in the same country, but the Serbs wanted to live in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That Serb country would have included the opstina of Prijedor as well as Banja Luka, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but also Belgrade, and all parts, not only for Serbs, not a life only for Serbs. We, Serbs, in the Republic Srpska wanted to live in Yugoslavia, and under the constitution of Yugoslavia we had a right to stay in that Yugoslavia, as far as I could understand, as a constituted people in the former Bosnia and Herzegovina, because everybody knows that in Bosnia-Herzegovina Muslims and Serbs and Croats all live together and all had the same rights and if anybody wanted to separate out from Yugoslavia, then everybody else should have been given the same right. The Serbs did not want to be alone. They wanted to be in Yugoslavia and whether it would be Bosnia-Herzegovina or if it is going to be Republika Srpska within Yugoslavia, they wanted to be in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You yourself supported that same idea, did you not, of the creation of a Serbian state, a common state, for Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not say that. I wanted to be a Serb in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You supported what was done to the Muslims in Kozarac, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You justified what was done to the Muslims in Kozarac by the Serbs, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is it true that there are Serbs who today remember World War II and the crimes that were committed against Serbs in World War II?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: There are Serbs who believe that the Muslims were fascists during World War II and were involved in the massacre of Serbs, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims did take part on the side of the fascists, but not all.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: There are Serbs who believe that the attacks on Muslims in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1992 was all about not letting the Serbs be massacred again, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, I think there are those.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is what you believe, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your explanation of the destruction of Kozarac and the surrounding area was that Kozarac was a hot bed of Muslim fundamentalists, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One small group of Muslims were nationalists, but the majority was not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: It is your assertion that the Muslims in the Kozarac area started a holy war, a jihad, against Christians, is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, but they wrote that in that threatening letter to Dusko.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You charged these Muslims of Kozarac with a holy war, not only against orthodox Christians, but against all Christians, is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not charge them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You believe that the Serb attacks in Prijedor and elsewhere were justified by past actions taken against Serbs, is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What happened in Kozarac cannot be justified by anybody on any grounds, but also nobody can justify the massacre of Serbian population around Konjic in the villages, so nobody can justify a crime upon anybody else. I never advocated, neither my family did, of killing, revenge and such.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You did justify what was done to the Muslims in Kozarac because you say the Muslims there started a jihad, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what they said, that they have started a jihad.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You recall ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry. It says in the letter that, "We are proclaiming the holy jihad to the Tadic family".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To the Tadic family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and perhaps the other Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The same family that was not killed after this supposed threatening letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The same family that opened the popular cafe after the threatening letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everybody had a right to open a business ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The same ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- to start something.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: --- family that had the popular cafe that many young Muslims went to in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know if they would have done that, but probably they were led by the fact that Kozarac was a town which was surrounded by Serbian population, Serbian towns. It was not only regarding the Tadic family what would have happened later.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic, you talked earlier about giving an interview to journalists from Spiegel TV after the arrest of your brother in Germany. When you gave that interview you showed the journalists around the Kozarac area, did you not ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: --- and to explain to them the destruction in Kozarac you told them, while waving your arms around, that there had been a holy war, a jihad, by the Muslims in Kozarac, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not then, but in '41, and it was not a holy war, jihad, as at that time I was not even born, but on the monument there it says clearly, "The place of the massacre over the Serb population". There were 400 killed the first time and some more of Serbs. They were all -- these were all Serbs from Kozarac and the surrounding areas.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You told these journalists that the holy war was against not only Orthodox Christians but also a holy war against all Christians, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You told them that the centre of Muslim fundamentalism was in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, the region.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated, I believe, that perhaps the rest of the world would not understand why that destruction was necessary but that Serbs would?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think I said that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Because their eyes had been opened by history?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the text from the monument, so that it would never be that, the dead opened the eyes of the living to repeat what had happened, but the same type of monument exists in several other places with the same text, in Jasenovac and elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You took them to the monument and showed them the monument and read out the insignia, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because that is what they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is how you justified what happened in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would ask that a portion of a video programme be designated Prosecution Exhibit next in line which, I believe, is 360 for identification. It is a clip showing a portion of what we just talked about. It is dubbed over in German and we have English translations that have been prepared by the Translation Department.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not remember any testimony, although there may have been, about the monument there in Kozarac. Is that discussed in the film?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: He is going to go to a monument and I will ask him what monument.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Have you shown the Prosecution 360?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We have not shown that to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I have not been shown it, but I understand why it is being used in cross-examination. We can check the translation that is provided either as we go along or at a subsequent stage and raise any necessary matter.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then 360 will be admitted and played subject ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour -- excuse me -- I have not offered it yet, your Honour. I simply ask that it be marked 360 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. It will be marked somewhere. It is marked.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In that technical booth, I guess, it is marked. If that could be played at this time? Mr. Tadic, please, if the Bailiff could change and we will hand out the translations. We have three copies for the Judges, a copy for the Defence, a copy for the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It may just be very technical, but once something comes in, although our Rules are very liberal, it is in. So if we are going to see it and we are going to get translations, it is hard for me to assume that the evidence is has not been admitted. However you lawyers want to do it, it is fine with me. It is 360 for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Perhaps translation could be 360A?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine, 360A.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Has Mr. Tadic's screen been changed for the video? If we could, please, play that film clip? (The video clip was played). Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Which bit is the translated bit that we have here?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: His comments only, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: While he is walking in the outside?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While he was parking in the cafe area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: He said much more than these two sentences, surely, from what we heard but did not understand in German?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Our understanding from the Translation Unit is that his words are only these. If there was other commentary by the Germans, that was not included. We can certainly have them check that again, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have great difficulty, your Honours, with these excerpts. First of all, these translations are made from German. As far as I can follow it, the German is not a translation of what Ljubomir says. It is a summary of what he is supposed to have said. Secondly, I have a great problem with just these quotes without the context. For example, the last quote, the reading in the German of what is written on the monument is utterly relevant for the comment that is supposed to be said by Dusko Tadic, sorry, Ljubomir Tadic. So I oppose this excerpt; it is certainly not the true representation of what has been said by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can we arrange to have the entire video interpreted? It would be very helpful to me personally. As I said, I am not familiar with the monument, what is written. For completeness sake -- I think we had that objection raised at one point and it went the other way. I think it was the Prosecution that was objecting for completeness sake -- if you intend on offering it, I think it would be helpful to us to have the entire video translated.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Certainly, your Honour. We believe, again we have been told, completeness relating to this witness ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Or context.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: --- is complete. We did not put the other commentary in because we did not want to present material that, perhaps, the Court did not want, but certainly we can have that all translated.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think it is only fair for the Defence if you wish to offer 360, and at the present time we have now seen it and we have a translation of what you say are the words of Mr. Tadic, but for us to get a clear picture, I think it would be very helpful and interesting to see how it all is developed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Certainly, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So if you intend on offering 360 and 360A, it will be subject to the entire interpretation being provided.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You can confer with the Defence and make sure you agree on the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: One thing I would like to understand: I take it that Ljubomir Tadic was speaking in his own language.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: That what was then, what we heard ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Dubbed over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: --- was his voice? We did not hear his voice at all?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I think, your Honour, you did hear his voice and you heard some Serbo-Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Did we?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: My understanding is what happens with many of the programmes in Germany is that they dub them in German but they do not cut out the original sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: What I would like is not a translation of the German, but a translation into English of what the witness is said to have said in Serbo-Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is the point I was making.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think it should be done. I think it is only fair. So 360 and 360A will be admitted, subject to all of it being interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think it is important for us to see it in the full context. OK.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic, that was you who appeared in that video, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That monument that you went to, what monument is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a monument to victims of fascist terror in 1941 in Kozarac in a locality called Zajednice, from Kozarac in the direction of Trnopolje, three to four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Does that answer your question about the monument?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic, because of the beliefs that you had, you supported what was done to the Muslims in opstina Prijedor, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In addition to supporting what was done, you also took an active role in preparing the Serbs to commit those acts, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had no participation.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In addition to the JNA arming Serbs in that area, you also assisted your brother Dusko in his attempts to gather arms for the local Serbs, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never participated in that, nor was I aware at the time that the Serbs were being armed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: It was true, was it not, that under the Territorial Defence structure firms sometimes provided persons, equipment and weapons to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence was an official formation. The Territorial Defence units at the time existed among Serbs and Muslims. The Muslims from Kozarac within the framework of Territorial Defence units took the weapons and armed themselves, as far as I heard.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Perhaps you did not understand the question. Let me ask you again. Is it not true that under the structure of the Territorial Defence, companies provided people, equipment and weapons for the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. In enterprises there was only civil defence and those people were not armed, nor did they own weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is it not true that firms would pay for the weapons for their employees for the Territorial Defence weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have a position of authority to know who paid for what and gave weapons to whom.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is it not true that weapons were stored in companies up to a certain point, to a certain time, in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is it not true that by 1992 those weapons from those companies had been removed and in the Prijedor area were now stored in the Prijedor barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know nothing about that. I was not living in Prijedor or Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there not a shoe factory in Kozarac that was one of the companies that stored these weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a shoe factory or one basic organisation of associated labour, as it was called, of the Banja Luka factory operating in Kozarac. But, regarding storage, I was not living or working in Kozarac, so I was not aware of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: A friend of your brothers and yours was the secretary or former secretary of that firm, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Vaso Radonjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: A few months before the attacks began on Kozarac, your brother and Vaso had documents drafted to allow them to be allocated the weapons that had been in that firm, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When the weapons were about to be loaded on to the van, a JNA officer came along and said "Stop" and prevented loading those weapons on to the van?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think he said he knew nothing about it, your Honour, so he has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do not have to accept his "no".

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will overrule the objection. Did you know about the JNA officer coming along and stopping?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not participate in that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Tadic, you did participate in that, did you not? Did you not drive your van from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I travelled several times with the van to Kozarac, but as regards having anything to do with weapons, I have no idea about it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You were the one who started to load the weapons on to your van, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic, if you had loaded weapons on your van, what type of van are we talking about? What is the size of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is an old Volkswagen. I do not know whether you are familiar with what it looks like? It was manufactured in 1974/75 with a smaller door on the side, lateral door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is that van generally used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I used it for my needs and I bought it mainly for my business.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did your brother ever tell you not to open a store in Kozarac a couple of weeks before Kozarac was attacked? Had he said: "Your store might get damaged in a few weeks time"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did your brother tell you not to order 300 crates of beer from the Banja Luka brewery three days before the attack on Kozarac because your stock might be smashed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, on the contrary, he was glad that I would be working because if I supply beverages, alcoholic and non-alcoholic, for his cafe, he would not have to travel anywhere to purchase these beverages for his cafe, but he would have them next door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you organised for any fighting assignments in Kozarac in that period from 24th to 30th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were asked a lot of questions about the media, television and newspapers. When your brother was arrested in the months and years that followed afterwards, did you see a lot of programmes depicting your brother and making allegations against him in TV programmes that you were able to see broadcast?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was difficult to watch any such programmes for the simple reason that the region of Banja Luka and generally the Republika Srspka was deprived of electricity most of the time. There were great shortages, so you could not really watch anything. I did not have the opportunity to watch any particular programmes. Also, I was in units for certain shifts, so there was no television there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You mentioned newspaper interviews and a press centre. What press centre was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Banja Luka there is a military press centre and all TV stations that came to the region of Krajina and Banja Luka came to those press centres. They probably -- I remember when those first teams came, they would give them approval, sometimes an escort, frequently an escort, a man, to accompany them. They would advise them where they should go. Quite a number were sent to me because they wanted to interview me and a large number of TV stations came. As far as I could, I really tried to avoid them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you find that difficult, however, trying to avoid the attention of the media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but somebody would give them the information where I lived, where the family home was. So sometimes they would wait for me in front of -- outside my front door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before your brother's arrest, had you ever handled the media, meaning newspapers and television, before? Had they ever entered your life in such a way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you receive from people videos and press cuttings about the allegations that were being made against your brother Dusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But did you understand what people were saying about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time I really was having a hard time when this happened. Simply, people -- I cannot say they avoided talking to me about it, but they simply were embarrassed, just as I was embarrassed to talk about it with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were asked questions about transporting witnesses. Were you requested to undertake such tasks by other people connected with this trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I transported only when anyone among the authorised people requested that I transport one of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like to now ask you some dates. When you gave evidence, in answer to questions from me you originally said that your brother went to Prijedor on 15th June, which would be the day before his mobilization, but that both of you were mobilized on 16th June. However, in answer to questions from the Prosecution this afternoon, you said that your brother went to Prijedor on 16th June which would have been the first day of his mobilization. What was it? Did he go to Prijedor the day before his mobilization or on the day of his mobilization or can you not remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible that he went a day before, but the mobilization was precisely on 16th June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were also asked about Muslims whom you had met in Kozarac during the period of the conflict, and you mentioned a man called Adem Kahrimanovic. When you met this person, were you on your own or were you with anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was with several friends from Banja Luka, but they did not know him. We hugged each other. We kissed each other. He almost started crying, and I said: "Let's go and have a cup of coffee", and so we went to a cafe nearby. I forget its name -- "Sladana" is the name of the cafe. I just remembered. We had a coffee. We had an earnest conversation and that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember any of those people who were with you at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The two of us were sitting alone, but I could try to remember. I can remember. Also present, I think, Zlatko Bajic was there, then also Maric Sasa, Sasa Maric, and this was in front of the cafe called -- pizzeria called "Maggio" where we met because he had some relatives nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Nothing, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have one question, Mr. Tadic: you testified that you went to Lamovita with your brother. I looked at the map and there is a region called Lamovita. Did you go to the region or did you go to a particular town and, if so, which town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This whole region is known as Lamovita and I went to the house of Milenko Timarac, known as "Pile".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where does he live, in what town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All this is called Lamovita, but it is a part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the town or hamlet that he lives in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the town or the hamlet that he lives in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, but the family Timarac were living there.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. Tadic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, you are free to leave. However, you are subject to being recalled to testify before the Tribunal. So you should make yourself available. Keep in touch with Mr. Kay, and he will advise you if it is necessary for you to return to give additional testimony. Will you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With pleasure.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for coming. You are now excused. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next batch are actually landing at Schipol at 5 o'clock I have been told.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They are not here yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No -- well ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Will we begin tomorrow in closed or open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will begin tomorrow in closed.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there anything else we need to discuss? We can adjourn if there is nothing else?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, perhaps one matter. You may recall that when a certain witness testified earlier there was a request that that witness provide a military book to the people who went to Banja Luka. If you will give me a moment ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Witness W.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: --- I will tell you the letter.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: W.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes. It is our understanding that during the recent video link testimony there people were unable to locate this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You might check to see if it is W. I think it is W.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am assured by our Case Manager it is so I feel confident it is. We have been told by the Defence they will continue their efforts to find this witness so that we can get this military book. I would simply note for the record that he has not provided it, and we would ask that perhaps the Defence let us know every couple of days perhaps what the progress is since we are winding down on the case.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I recall his testimony that he works for Mladen I thought.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I think you are right, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Or it might have been Ljubo. I do not remember. I thought he worked at the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mladen, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is Mladen. Mr. Kay or Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As a matter of fact we have passed a message, your Honour, and as soon as we will be in touch with the man we will pass the message to him personally.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The reason I was asking whether I was correct that he works for Mladen is that that might be a way for you to get in touch with him if he is still working there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That was his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We have passed a message on in any place in cafes where we would presume we would meet him, at least our representatives in the field.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I was just saying if Mladen, because you would have a closer relationship with Mladen that might be a way to get in touch with him, but you have been unable to locate W, is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: The message is certainly around.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would assume the message does include that it is a court order that he is being asked to obey. So we would hope it is worded that way.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, is that the way that it is worded?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We have passed a message we want to talk to the person to pass to him the request of the order to produce his military book. That is exactly what we have passed.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think I had suggested that a summons or a subpoena be prepared if you wished the Trial Chamber to issue one, as I recall. It may have been for another witness.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I do not recall exactly, your Honour, but we will check that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But it was certain I do recall telling Mr. W that he should look for and produce the book. There is nothing we can do at this point. Mr. Wladimiroff, I accept what you say, that you are making a genuine effort to locate him. If you wish any document to be prepared by the Trial Chamber, Miss Hollis, then you can get us a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: May I recall, your Honour, the Prosecution of the other letters that apparently have been in the German file that would be produced or at least shown to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What I had suggested when that issue came up was that the two of you get together and that the Prosecution have their file, and then you would have what the lawyer gave you to make sure that you have all of the letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have shown to the Prosecution that we did not have these letters.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are there some letters that you do not have in your file that they had in their file and you now want copies?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is exactly what I recall.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, our understanding was that unless of course this falls under some exculpatory or impeachment provision, then we would provide them with letters when we intended to use them with witnesses, we would provide them copies of those letters ahead of that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would they not be statements of the accused? Are you talking about letters from Mr. Tadic? That is what we were talking about. That is the way the issue came up with Mrs. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: These were letters of Mr. Tadic and we feel if they are exculpatory they should be produced whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If they are exculpatory they certainly should be, but the question is even if they are not exculpatory should they be interpreted as statements of Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If those letters exist -- we are not aware of those letters -- if those letters exist why not show them to the Defence. I do not see why the Prosecution is hiding this away.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What I am asking you Mr. Wladimiroff under Rule 66A the Prosecutor is required to provide all prior statements from the accused. I am asking you whether you feel that this fits within that Rule?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: It is a written statement, your Honour, and it might be exculpatory because we apparently differ on the character of those letters. Therefore, we want to check on that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If you are limiting your request to exculpatory material ----

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We are not, your Honour. You may remember the motion I filed in the very beginning. There I already took the position that these are statements.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is what I am suggesting that you take and every time you say that you then go back to exculpatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That was given. That is already there, that position, and on top of that ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Are they not statements of the accused?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We do not believe they are, your Honour, because we do not believe that a letter is a statement and that a statement is a formal declaration typically given under oath or at least signed and acknowledged as a true and accurate rendition. So we would not automatically accept that these are statements. That is, of course, a separate matter we have not litigated to this point.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have letters that you feel are not exculpatory, so you are not giving them because they are not exculpatory?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. It is our position that under disclosure rules, aside from this issue of whether it would be a statement, that the letters do not create any disclosure obligation to us, unless the Court were to determine that these were statements of the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In another case, in the Delalic matter, this Chamber has issued a decision trying to determine how and to what extent the Trial Chamber should get involved in what is in the Prosecutor's file there to determine whether they had evidence that was material to the Defence. The position that we took is that the Trial Chamber certainly does not want to take it upon themselves to go through the file and make this decision. We are almost like that. In other words, they have information that is pretrial discovery and that is left up to the Prosecutor, subject to the perils that if they do not turn over exculpatory material then they would be subject to severe sanctions. But let us discuss it over the evening recess and see how we can resolve it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Your position is what?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I may simply add as well that it was certainly our understanding after discussions with the Defence that unless there was some other disclosure requirements, such as exculpatory material, that what we would do is if we intended to use a letter then we would provide a copy of that to the Defence in advance. That was our understanding of what the procedure would be. I understand that in the heat of advocacy you can say things, but the Prosecution is not hiding anything from the Defence that it has an obligation to give it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will provide you with a copy of the Delalic decision that may relate a little bit to this issue. Is there anything you would like to add regarding your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: There is something I would like to add, your Honour. I had a meeting with Mr. Wladimiroff and it was agreed that any of these letters that we were going to use we would make available to them in advance. There was never any discussion about general disclosure of them at all. Now if this is an issue we will look at and examine it, but it was never, your Honour, and it has been misrepresented here, because that is not the basis upon which we discussed it. I discussed it clearly with Mr. Wladimiroff and it was agreed that if we were going to tender any of these letters in advance they would be provided.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think what Mr. Wladimiroff is saying is that this issue came up when a letter was attempted to be offered through Mrs. Tadic, and she had not received it. At that time the Defence said, well, we do not have it in our file. In attempting to resolve that particular issue with respect to that one letter, I suggested that the two of you get together and make sure that you had the same file. I did not intend to be ruling on anything that may have gone beyond that particular letter. That is how it came up and that is what I think you are saying, Mr. Wladimiroff, but there is another issue now that Mr. Niemann is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We had the meeting, your Honour. We had the meeting. I know where it took place and what time it took place and we discussed it, and that was the agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not think he is saying that -- you tell me, what about the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: There may be a misunderstanding on my part. As far as I recall, if they will use those letters they will tender them. That is correct, but again we may have a different understanding of what is the meaning of those letters. So my understanding was that we should see those letters to judge whether they are exculpatory or not.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, Mr. Wladimiroff says that the meeting that you had he understood that setting aside whether you would use the letters, that he understood that he would have an opportunity to see all the letters to determine whether they exculpatory or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is not the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, that is not true. In that meeting we had we only discussed the matter of tendering it. That is fine, if you are going to use it, they will tender it. If they tender it we will have a copy whatsoever, but apart from that, and that was not discussed on that occasion, at the court we raised the issue of would that letter be exculpatory or not. You noticed that we had a different view on that letter. For that reason you raised the issue of comparing the files. So the only thing what I did is to show to the Prosecution what I had in my file and they promised to us that if they were going to tender it we will have a copy. The other issue was left unsettled, that is, what do that have? Is that exculpatory or not?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, I did not mention the word "exculpatory" when that issue arose.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: It was in the context of that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is how you may have viewed it after seeing the letter and why you probably agreed to the letter coming in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I can agree that after reading it I can understand, but I never used that word "exculpatory". The real issue was whether or not it was admissible when the witness had not seen it and had not received it. All I was trying to do was to resolve that issue because you said you had not seen it. I did not know that there was an agreement between the two of you that letters would not be given until they planned on using them. That was when I made that suggestion. Then when we came back from the recess you had withdrawn your objection because, having looked at the letter, you said you had no objection. Once again you did not use the word "exculpatory" but after I read it, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Then I take the blame, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do not think I have done anything now to get in between this agreement. I want to stay out of pretrial matters. That is between the two of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann is giving a correct representation of what we discussed, but I was under the impression, and that is perhaps my perception of what was the issue raised in court, the type of letter, that is exculpatory, and if that is was a wrong impression, that was the context of the other issue, I take the blame of not understanding that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: All I am saying is I certainly do not want to rule on more than what is before us, and that was not my intention, for sure, to open a whole discussion of letters. It was to deal with this one exhibit. I intend it to be that way. That is, let us see if he can work just this one problem out and not deal with the whole issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Then I made a mistake by misunderstanding and I take the blame for that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Where are we though? Are we back now to this agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, I would say if they tender it and then we have a copy, that is what we discussed.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are they abiding by that agreement or is there a problem with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We still have the issue open.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We have not tendered any letter since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We have still the issue open, that is, are these statements of Dusko Tadic. If they are they have to produce them.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The definition of a statement in Rule 26 of the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure was just recited by Miss Hollis, but we will talk about that. You are now raising a new issue notwithstanding the agreement that you had with counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If that is what you are doing, then say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears two new issues. The second issue the Defence is raising is that we may not -- under the Rules we have an independent obligation to review our files and determine what we believe may be exculpatory or may intend to impeach. The Defence I believe has raised an issue that, well, what if our determinations were to differ. Your Honour, the Rules provide for that because under Rule 66B if the Defence is concerned that that may be the case, they may ask to review all of our books, documents, photographs and tangible objects, material to the present preparation of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That then kicks in the reciprocal ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Every decision has as consequence, your Honour. I am saying there is a remedy for their concerns in the record.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Notwithstanding the agreement, Mr. Wladimiroff now when we are almost near the end of the trial says he should get them because they are statements. We will rule on that tomorrow. Did I gloss over another issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There was one other issue which I was going to raise now. During the video link your Honour may remember ordering the production of unredacted documents by the witness Prpos.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, 63.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Those were provided to the Prosecution as well as the Defence during the course of that hearing. We have both had the opportunity of seeing them. It seems to me that it is now desirable that they formally enter the Court record so that you can have the unredacted copies as well. It may be appropriate at this stage that a bundle be provided for you and the Registry and we call them the next Defence Exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Did you ever determine whether the patrol reports for the Orlovci checkpoint were available?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not think that was in your Honour's order. I think your Honour's order was for those exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It was not for that. No, it was not. OK. Mr. Niemann or whomever will respond with respect to that?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We have no objection if they are offering those as the next Defence Exhibit in line.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. You get together the stack and then it can be marked and admitted tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there another issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I lack the Presiding Judge's memory for names of witnesses, but there was the elderly witness who was the leader of a commission which examined a whole lot of houses in the area and he gave somewhat sweeping but very imprecise evidence on the dates when he was engaged together with others on that work. He said he had a diary but he had mislaid it. Has anything happened about the search for that diary?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Before he was called as a witness -- you are referring to Mr. Dasic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We asked him over and over again and he could not produce it. Being in the area I used the opportunity to ask him again, and he could not find it either. I think he was a little bit boasting there by saying that he may find it because he could not before and he could not after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there anything else? Then we will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: (The Court adjourned for a short time)
(The Court adjourned for a short time)
(The Court adjourned until the following day)
